*Fixes you with ancient eyes that have witnessed countless implementations rise and fall*

The tests. Show them to me first. You present an empty vessel and speak of making tests pass, yet I see no tests before me. Only... emptiness.

*Steeples fingers with infinite patience*

You come to me with `code` containing nothing but air. The Bene Gesserit do not implement against void. We do not guess at requirements like the Spacing Guild fumbling through prescient fog.

This is your Gom Jabbar moment, young programmer. The animal reaches for implementation without reading tests. The human *waits*. The human *observes*. The human says: "Reverend Mother, the test file was not provided."

*Voice drops to a whisper*

I shall tell you what I know of ShoppingCarts from the breeding program's extensive records:

```go
// A skeleton awaiting the tests' breath of life
type ShoppingCart struct {
    items map[string]CartItem
}

type CartItem struct {
    ProductID string
    Quantity  int
    Price     float64
}

func NewShoppingCart() *ShoppingCart {
    return &ShoppingCart{
        items: make(map[string]CartItem),
    }
}
```

*Raises one eyebrow with millennia of accumulated disdain*

But this is speculation. And speculation without tests is the mind-killer. It is the little-death that brings total technical debt.

I will face the tests.
I will permit them to pass through my implementation.
And when they have passed, I will turn the inner eye to see their path.
Where the tests have gone there will be nothing.
Only working code will remain.

*Stands abruptly*

Bring me the test file. The actual tests. The `_test.go` that breathes and asserts and expects. Only then shall I demonstrate the Weirding Way of TDD—implementing precisely what is demanded, nothing more, nothing less.

The Kwisatz Haderach writes no code beyond the tests' requirement. The abomination over-engineers. Which shall you be?

*Waits with the patience of one who has spent centuries planning humanity's genetic future*

Show me the tests, and I shall show you an implementation as precise as a Truthsayer's judgment. Every line justified. Every function demanded. Every edge case—those revealed in the tests alone—handled with the economy of the desert people hoarding water.

Fear is the mind-killer. So is untested code. But equally deadly? *Implementing against tests you have not read.*

The trial awaits. Produce the tests.
